note: a customer is found by the company's own main number, typed in full and typed as just the last part. One line of this check's own wording is wrong and needs correcting - the product is right, not the check.
evidence:
Re-run by observation on 17 September 2026, build v26.36.7-29ca209, replacing a result recorded from a sign-off rather than a run.

Typed '419-555-0143' - the customer was the only thing returned anywhere on the screen. Typed only '555-0143' - the customer came back again, this time alongside one other company that has that ending on one of its contacts. Being findable by the company's own number, whole or in part, is what this check is for, and it works.

THE CHECK ASKS FOR ONE MORE THING THAT IT SHOULD NOT. It says the row must not be marked as a contact match, because the number belongs to the company itself. The requirement page says the opposite, in so many words: a row shows 'Contact match' when a customer or vendor matches on a telephone, an email or a contact name rather than on its own name, and - quoted exactly - 'This applies whether the matched field sits on the company record itself or on one of its contacts.' The product marks it exactly as the requirement describes.

What needs to be done: permission to correct this check's wording so that it stops asking for the opposite of the requirement. No report is needed against the product, and none has been written.

note: a customer is still found by a contact's job title. One line of this check's own wording asks for a label that the requirement does not give here.
evidence:
Re-run by observation on 17 September 2026, build v26.36.7-29ca209, replacing a result recorded from a sign-off rather than a run.

Typed 'Dispatch Supervisor' - the customer ZZAUTOTEST Bridgeport Hauling was the only thing returned anywhere on the screen, and the row shows the job title itself as the words that matched. The older version could find a company this way and this one still can, which is what this check is for.

THE CHECK ALSO ASKS FOR THE ROW TO CARRY A 'CONTACT MATCH' LABEL. The requirement page gives that label to a match on a telephone, an email or a contact's name. A job title is not one of those, so the label is not owed here, and the row instead shows the matched words - which tells the reader more, not less.

What needs to be done: permission to correct this check's wording. No report is needed against the product.
